question: Which of the following pairs is an example of 'molecule of an element itself'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen gas and oxygen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Molecules of an element** are composed of two or more atoms of the same element chemically bonded together. Examples include **hydrogen gas (H₂)** and **oxygen gas (O₂)**.
 
• In hydrogen gas (**H₂**), two hydrogen atoms share electrons to form a covalent bond, creating a diatomic molecule. This is a classic example of a molecule of an element.
 
• Similarly, oxygen gas (**O₂**) consists of two oxygen atoms bonded together via a double covalent bond, forming another diatomic molecule of an element.
